summary.7-10: God makes everything, and it is good.
summary.11-14: God speaks, and a world appears.
summary.15-18: The Bible's opening claim about where everything comes from.

7-10: At the very beginning there was no sky, no sea, no trees and no people. There was only God.
God spoke. He said, “Let there be light” — and there was light. Day after day he made more: sky and sea, land and plants, the sun and the moon, fish and birds and animals.
Last of all he made people. He looked at everything he had made and said it was very good. Then he rested.
11-14: Genesis opens with nothing that anyone could photograph: darkness, water, and God. Then God speaks, and things begin to exist that did not exist before.

The making has a shape. First God makes spaces — light and dark, sky and sea, dry land. Then he fills them — sun and moon, birds and fish, animals and people. Nothing is an accident and nothing is left over.
People come last, made in God's image, given the job of looking after the rest. And then God stops, and calls the whole thing good.
15-18: Genesis 1 is written as ordered poetry rather than as a laboratory report, and its shape is deliberate: days one to three form the realms, days four to six fill them, and the seventh day crowns the sequence with rest.

Read next to the creation stories of Israel's neighbours, the differences are pointed. There is no battle between gods, no accidental universe, and no monstrous sea to be defeated — the sea is simply made. The sun and moon, worshipped everywhere around Israel, are not even named; they are called lamps.

Humanity is made in God's image — a phrase used elsewhere in the ancient world for kings and for statues of gods — and given to every person, male and female alike. Then comes the seventh day, when God rests, not from exhaustion but as a declaration that the work is finished and good.

whatHappened.7-10: God made the whole world by speaking, and he made people last of all.
whatHappened.11-14: God created the world in an ordered way, made people in his own image, and called it all good.
whatHappened.15-18: God creates by word, in ordered sequence, and pronounces the result good — a claim about the origin, the goodness and the purpose of everything that exists.

whatItTeaches.7-10: Everything around you was made on purpose — including you.
whatItTeaches.11-14: The world is not an accident, and neither are you. If God made it good, then looking after it matters.
whatItTeaches.15-18: If creation is by intention and declared good, then material things matter, work matters, rest matters, and every human being carries a dignity nobody granted and nobody can revoke.

thinkAboutIt.7-10: What is your favourite thing that God made? Why do you think he made it?
thinkAboutIt.11-14: If God called the world good, what does that mean for how you treat it — and how you treat yourself?
thinkAboutIt.15-18: If every person carries God's image, who does that make it impossible for you to look down on?

pray.7-10: Thank you God for making the world, and for making me. Help me look after what you made.
pray.11-14: God, you made everything on purpose, including me. Help me treat your world, and the people in it, as good.
pray.15-18: God, you spoke and there was light. Teach me to treat what you called good as good — the world, other people, and myself.

prompt.11-14: What is created on the first day?
prompt.15-18: What is created on day one, and why is that ordering significant?

explain.11-14: Light — the sun does not appear until day four.
explain.15-18: Light precedes the luminaries, which demotes the sun and moon from deities to created lamps.
